tips.comment: This S Dixon-trained 6-year-old gelding is in good form, winning his previous two races over seven furlongs at this course. He missed out on his hat-trick bid when only beaten a neck in second behind the T Faulkner-trained First Greyed over one mile seven days ago. So, from a two-pound lower mark and with D Swift onboard, another big run looks likely.
Late headway on reappearance run last time and will be fitter for the run. Billy The Kid back on top and there is money for this one.
This horse won nicely last time out and has only gone up 2 lb in the handicap. Plus, it has been known to put a few good runs together, and today looks like he will get a nice pace to run at.

That's My Boy Luke goes at Southwell and has shown a bit in patches. He was a good second here over a mile a while back and wasn’t far off again at Newcastle not long after. Form’s been a bit up and down since, but he’s off a workable mark and knows his way around the all-weather. If he bounces back to that earlier form, he’s got a squeak in this.

Interesting that they won a class 5 on penultimate start @ Newcastle after a 66 day break and have had that same length of break here in this class 6. Retains a decent mark of 65 today, under used jockey up and very shrewd trainer best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ his local track, making current 20/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Timetobenice goes back up in trip and that could be the key to unlocking a big run. He’s already got a win on the board and ran a strong second earlier in the year, so the ability’s there. His last couple haven’t quite gone to plan over shorter but this longer distance should suit him a lot better.

Tasmanian Legend might be up to running a big race in this. The selection has won three times in the past and has won at this trip. The selection was down the field at Chelmsford last time but might do better in this company.
Light Up Our Stars has a strong track record with 9 wins and 8 places on similar going. He is a consistent competitor especially with headgear.

In terrific form and no sign that the form is dropping. Should handle the extra furlong on this track. Aiden Brooks' three-pound claim looks significant. Won here two runs back and a repeat is on the cards.

Match Anthem has been in solid form lately with two wins and a couple of good placed runs since then. He’s clearly thriving on the all-weather and keeps showing up with honest efforts. Stays the trip well, handles different tracks, and if he turns up in the same mood again he should be right in the thick of it.

Race 7 at Southwell today is the Boost Your Acca At BetMGM Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,421 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 11-year-old gelding Mr Slicker from the Sarah Hollinshead yard, and will be ridden by Joe Leavy. This remarkable son of Exceed and Excel is an 8-time winner from 94 starts and is still showing all the enthusiasm in the world for racing with consistency of note. He is well overdue for his next win, but in this field, he looks a good thing and has the form to back up those claims.

Has a disturbing habit of being slowly away, but Cam Hardie knows the horse well. He should really have won more often than the seven times he has to date, three on turf. This is not a fantastic race, but you have a number of horses who are regularly putting it down without winning. I am still going with the selection, who, if he can get his act together, is a shade better.

Now Lumenbourg has come out, EMBARKED is the likely front runner and that scenario could pay off here. Gets Taryn Langley back in the saddle, and she got close from five pounds higher in the weights on consecutive runs over this trip in January and February. We've stuck with this one for a while now, so bear that in mind, but can't be ruled out in case he returns back in that mood.
Cubanista has shown flashes of ability but if he can recapture his earlier performance levels, he could be competitive in this field.

Looks very interesting dropping back in trip after finishing a cracking 1L 3rd of 9 to 'Overnight Oats' over today's course (1m 13yds) on the AW in a Class 5 Handicap earlier this month. It looks like the one to be on in this open-looking race off the same mark.

Twilight Diamond looks an interesting one here after showing plenty of speed last time out over course and distance. He made a bold bid from the front, only fading late on, and now makes his handicap debut off a mark of 75. That effort suggests he’s got a bit about him and with natural improvement, he could go very close.

Dark Side Thunder is one that might give us a decent run here. The selection was fourth here last time but might well have needed that run and has winning form over course and distance. It is likely to run a big race again here.

All of his last 3 wins have come here over CD, including 2 runs ago. He was stepped up to 7f here 28 days ago but finished 5th of 7. So today's return back to 6f for local trainer Roy Bowring's charge should suit, and the claimer taking 3lb off is an added bonus.

Kats Bob has been knocking on the door lately and got his reward with a win at Newcastle a few runs back. He’s been super consistent over 6f on the all-weather and clearly enjoys this sort of setup. He’s holding his form well and if he gets the right run through, there’s every chance he’s right there again at the finish. Reliable type who’s hard to rule out.

One More Dream won this race last year off an official rating of 79 and now is rated 12 lb lower than that and is expected to take advantage of it here to go close to doubling up under Jason Hart. Last time out was shown to be in decent form when 4th of 9 over course and distance just under three weeks ago, beaten just under two lengths, battling for 2nd up until the final stages. If the introduction of blinkers settles matters, coupled with the drop in weights, it could well be telling here.

Hierarchy has not won for 21 runs but has been mostly consistent and placed in those. As a result, it is very attractively handicapped and should be competitive if the race is run to suit, and it could well be.

Kamakameleon is a 2yo colt trained by Dylan Cunha. He is out of 2000 Guineas winner Kameko. The trainer won this race last year with Zminiature, and his entrant Kamakameleon is out of a dam that won at Leopardstown as a 2yo and placed in a Group 3 as a 2yo. The owners have had one other horse, a 2yo, that finished 3/20 in a valuable Harry's Goffs Million at York last year, with Sensorium bagging £61k. It's likely Kamakameleon is primed and ready on debut and is my short-priced banker of the day.

Sucking Diesel is a half-sister to a decent sort over sprint trips, and this yard has produced plenty of decent juveniles early in the past couple of seasons. She should be well forward and can run a massive race here.

This is a large field of unraced 2 year olds so it's down to breeding and following the money. This horse is one of four for Roger Fell. He is bred for speed and has attracted support in the early betting exchanges.

Harswell Calling is another 2-year-old trained by Roger Fell in this race. On jockey bookings, this looks at first glance to be the stable's number one, but the odds are huge. The selection is speedily bred and can hopefully outrun its odds in a large field of unraced 2-year-olds.

Looks a great price and one of the only horses in the field who doesn't seem to have major concerns. Others may be unfit and won't suit the trip/going. I've valued it to 5/1 and William Hill are offering 8/1 with 6 places.

Winner in this class last season, 3/4 in handicaps, gelded since and looks progressive. Only a 4-year-old, so likely to improve from last season, and with 7 places available, 1/5 is worth a go each way.

Won this race last year from 1lb higher, so surely will be primed here for the repeat. Not disgraced from a higher mark last season, including 7th in the Cambridgeshire from 7lbs higher. Looks a great each-way price.

Doesn't look like there's loads of pace on offer here, with only a few prominent runners down the center. Myal makes his seasonal reappearance on an upward curve, having won his last 5, including over 7f here last season. Won cosily that day from a mark of 82, and with the 2nd and 4th both winning on their next start, an 8lbs rise doesn't seem out of reach. Likely to blast off, and with not a great deal of pace on offer, he could make it stick from the front.

A seemingly wide-open Spring Mile, and a chance taken here on Rogue Encore, who found a jolt of improvement when switched to the AW with 3 good runs in quick succession in November with cheekpieces applied. Royal Zabeel puts real gloss on the form of his latest effort, given he is now rated 111 and didn’t beat this horse far receiving 2 lbs. The Rogue's horse has a bit to prove back on turf, but I’d be hopeful the retained cheekpieces can see him continue an upward curve and prove well handicapped off 84 towards the bottom of these weights. Hopefully, he can get a nice drag into the race by Naepoint despite not being drawn the best in a mid to high draw. The trainer has an in-form jockey booked who has 14 winners from 37 rides in March.

A progressive 4yo who has won or been placed in 9 of 14 races. Coming off a 4 month break but the yard is having a very good year so far and he should be ready. A good apprentice in the saddle whose 5lb claim is a big plus. The recent break and a gelding op could easily bring about more improvement.

Cynosure could be the one to provide quite a major upset here. Disappointing in the synthetic last time out, but on this track is likely to find better form. Good jockey-trainer combination and is better than that last run suggested.
Trainer Clive Cox will have done a lot of work with the very talented sprinter James's Delight. He looks a worthy favourite today.
Second in this race last season and comes into this on the back of three solid runs on the all-weather, so will not lack fitness.

Al Shabab Storm looks the best value in the field by a mile. With the market leader and the 2nd favorite looking like they won't be fully fit, this has a value price of 7/2, and 9/1 is an absolute steal. Looks like one of the best bets of the day. May go double stakes for this one as it will go in closer to the race.

May not be fit to run, but even with the fitness concerns, I've priced it to 13/8, and 11/4 is up for grabs. Looks a cracking bet at the price and is well ahead of this lot. Also reckon it's very unexposed and has potential for a lot more.

The 4-year-old is coming off a 5-month break, but he was a close 2nd of 13 in a French Group 1 race on his return last year. Things did not really go to plan after, finishing 6th of 16 in the Derby and 4th of 12 in a quality Group 1 when last seen. He’s had time to get his act together and can be a big player at this Listed level.

I can't work out why, but Point Lynas looks to have been overlooked by the racing press. Rated 112, the 6-year-old is not here for a day out. Perhaps he would like the ground a little firmer in an ideal world.

3 wins from 6 starts. Won a Class 2 handicap at York on good to firm last August. Only 1 run since, when fourth in a Class 2 handicap at Ascot on soft, both over 1 mile. Only 4lb higher than the York win. Progressive and could be better than a handicapper this season.
Second last time out over course and distance. Has won over the distance twice last season at Nottingham and Newmarket. Now running for a new stable. Going today will suit.

I've priced Native Warrior at 7/2, and they are offering 10/1. However, I believe the fitness concerns may hinder its chances. Nearly the whole field has fitness concerns as they are all going off very fresh. Ones that have had a run will have an advantage, but Native Warrior is a lot classier than its mark suggests.

Orandi looks a cracking bet here as it's had a run at the Curragh and it looks well handicapped to the conditions. No fitness concerns, unlike the others near the top of the market, and going off fit will surely ensure it at least gets into the placings. I have priced it to 8/1, and 11/1 is of course bigger, so I'm going to take the value in the big race of the day.

He finished last season with two nice runs and two 100+ RPR ratings. He went very close on the AW three weeks ago, after a 5 month break, and his well-being seems fine. No problem with the slower ground. On a decent mark. Few miles on the clock for the 4yo and plenty of room for more progress.

Was 2nd in this race last year and was also a cracking 2nd in the Balmoral Handicap from 2 lbs lower. Relishes these types of races and goes well fresh. Only having 5th start for the Camacho stable, so there could be more improvement.

A lack of pace in here if you believe the pace maps, which does make it a bit more of a mess than it would otherwise be anyway. After much deliberation, I was minded to give Orne a swing on handicap debut here. His best form would have him well handicapped off 97 anyway, but with an added 5lb claim from Luke Catton, I thought an adjusted 92 was of real interest for one that should be forward enough. On the face of it, the trip is a question mark, as the horse's career has gone the wrong way over 6f. That said, he was a decent 2.5L 2nd when splitting two horses now rated 107 and 109 respectively off level weights over a mile at Chelmsford. Indeed, he's placed on 3 of 5 runs at the trip, and granted not got his head in front, but some of those were at the highest level so can be forgiven. Ground should be fine for him, and with him being just 1lb off bottom weight, hopefully that can see him home well.
Dashing Darcey has the right profile to run a big race in the Lincoln. A 4-year-old carrying the right weight, making a seasonal debut after some very good win and placed efforts last term.

Sean is now an eight-year-old and has not won since he was trained and running in Italy in 2023. But after joining Jamie Osborne, he has spent his winters racing at Meydan in the UAE and placed in Group races in 2024. He was 4th twice in Group 2 races and a close 2nd of 16 in a handicap off his Lincoln mark of 102. He was also 2nd in an Ascot mile handicap last July off 106 and could go well in the Lincoln.

A very interesting looking class 5 maiden stakes race with my vote going to Kuredu King a highly promising gelded son of Churchill & Orcia ( Dam's sire the very smart Shamardal ) twice raced and showed good signs of promise on his first career start failed to build on that when last seen at Newcastle 142 days ago where finishing 10/12 however a line is best drawn over that as he had excuses on the occasion and he remains a good prospect for this season and is the type to do much better as a 3yo worth noting he cost 300,000 gns as a yearling stepping up in trip here a good move by his connections as it can bring out further in him jockey Kieren Shoemark takes the ride and can give John & Thady Gosden's inmate a promising ride here at Doncaster price at the time of writing looks of good value in my point of view and must be taken seriously and accordingly . Respected .

Looks the best value in the race. I've priced it at 4/1, so taking this price is great each way value, especially for 5 places. It has a great chance at this mark and could run off with the race due to others around it having major concerns. It is a big field, so it may need a little luck in running to win the race, but I don't think there's any stopping it from getting into the frame.
Good winner two starts back and from a good yard. Likely to improve with the latest outing when fourth. A win would be a minor upset in this field.

The 4yo has 1 win from 7. Progressed nicely last year, running well in defeat and not beaten far when last seen in a useful £52K turf handicap. Improvement possible after 5 months off the track. Weighted to go well and strong jockey booking. Question marks against most of these rivals.

Balding is currently at a 21% strike rate. He won at this level at Ascot last season under Haley with Burdett Road back in 5th. He was beaten the next time in the Old Rowley Cup when conceding 12 lbs to the winner Sun God, 4 lengths back to 3rd. He travelled into that unbelievably well, and it'll probably turn out the winner was very well weighted there. Dropping back to 1m3f is possibly a good move too, and he has to be the one to side with here.

Unbeaten in two 12f handicap starts here, winning impressively both times, and is back to just 1lb higher than the last winning mark here in January 2024. Seems to prefer this surface but was not disgraced last year on turf, especially when 8th in the Coral Handicap at Goodwood from 4lbs higher. Sure to be primed for this.

Unexposed 4yo. Four career runs, form 2213. Two narrow defeats at this track to start his career. A 9L turf maiden win on his third start. Posted a good RPR rating when last seen, which was a decent class 2 turf handicap. Nice mark, 7 months off the track but could have a decent future.
Grey Cuban could show more improvement this season. He bolted up by over 8L on his all-weather debut at Wolverhampton last April after being off course for 183 days.

I want to take on Soprano first time up as she needed her first couple of runs last year before getting better and better, and she's had quite a bit of racing now. Shuwari was highly rated and a one-time Guineas hope before an injury saw her miss her Classic year. However, she's still just 3 lbs behind Soprano on ratings, and this doesn't look too tricky a contest to start her off. If she's going to take top order amongst the fillies, she should be winning or going very close in this, despite the absence, and her stable have been in good form recently with 2 winners from 7 runners (also 2x 2nds and 1x 3rd).

Trained at Newmarket by Comrad Allen, Mercury Day is worth an each-way bet at odds of 100/1. To be fair, Comrad's camp is just looking for some black type for their stable flagship filly, and they would be ecstatic with just a 3rd place.
Undefeated in her two races American Gal arrives here today with plenty of promise. She is up in grade on her season return, however, at odds of 11/1 a chance can be taken with her.

Course and distance winner who was last seen bouncing back to form at Southwell 58 days ago where finishing 3rd/9 and this class 3 handicap looks a suitable looking assignment that should be run suit given the horses enrolled to run here currently operating on an unchanged mark of 90 it is very well possible that B R Millian's inmate has more to offer jockey Oisin Murphy takes the ride that being a positive and he can give Amazonian Dream a good ride here at Kempton merits consideration

Well bred colt by Galileo & Timbuktu ( Dam's sire Fastnet Rock ) who is thrice raced with a good win to his name already was last seen at Southwell 36 days ago where finishing a 3rd/8 and makes his handicap debut here of a mark of 83 and with plenty more improvement due on the cards John & Thady Gosden's inmate can rapidly begin to progress heading down the handicap route and he does appeal as the type to do so the blinkers are applied for the time here and they can have a positive effect jockey Oisin Murphy takes the ride and he can give Java Raja the perfect ride here at Kempton must be considered
Doctor Kildare has some very useful form and should be good enough to take this race. The trainer remains in good form and the step up in trip should suit.

Chase debutant. Given a mark of 112. He has some useful hurdling form to his name. He finished a decent 3rd behind Push The Button on hurdling debut. That horse is rated 135. He was then pitched into a Grade 2 next time out but finished a beaten 6th. He managed to get his head in front at Market Rasen, beating New Order comfortably. He's not shown anything in his 3 runs since. To be fair, it was always about chasing with this lad. He won 1 of his 2 point-to-point runs comfortably, beating Sound And Fury by a wide margin. That horse is rated 124 under rules, whereas this lad is only rated 112. If he can show that point-to-point form over fences, he's got plenty to give off this type of mark. The trainer does very well with his chase runners at this track. Profitable to back them blindly.

This looks like a potentially very informative bumper with a number of likely types on breeding, including Mr Jukebox and The Bluesmaster. But at the prices, I will have to have an each way bet on Mini Mario, who is by the sire of the moment, Blue Bresil, and is out of the high-class mare Marias Benefit, who won 8 races for this trainer up to Grade 2 standard.

Kayce Dutton is due a change of luck following a couple of runs in which being hampered by fallers, etc., more or less finished his chances. Confidence is tempered somewhat as the Pogsons' 7yo has to prove himself away from Huntingdon, so a small bet is advised.
